# Results — Study 287 (Easter-Effect) on the ^GSPC daily tape

computed by the Computus (anonymous Gregorian) algorithm; the surrounding ^GSPC
trading sessions are frozen in [`data.py`](../easter_effect/data.py) (1950–2025, 76
weekends). ^GSPC daily close-to-close returns (price-only) are from the repo-level
cache `_cache/^GSPC_split_only.parquet`. Match the fingerprints below to confirm
you hold the same data. As-of **2026-06-18**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n observations | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| ^GSPC daily close-to-close (price-only) — pre-holiday session (Maundy Thursday) | 1950–2025 | 76 events | `2b3e2834cdbc` |

## The setup — Good Friday is a market holiday

Good Friday (= Easter Sunday − 2 days) has been an NYSE holiday in every one of these
76 years, so there is **no "Good Friday return" to measure**. The natural event study
brackets the closed day with two real sessions:

- **Pre-holiday session** — the last trading day before Good Friday, which is *always*
  Maundy Thursday (weekday 3 in all 76 years). This is the textbook **pre-holiday
  effect** (Ariel 1990; Lakonishok & Smidt 1988).
- **Post-holiday session** — the first trading day after Easter Sunday, which is
  *always* Easter Monday (weekday 0 in all 76 years).

## The unconditional daily mean — the key baseline

The honest baseline is **not** zero. The S&P 500 drifts up a hair every session: the
unconditional daily mean over 1950–2025 is **+0.0364%/day** (≈3.6 bps), σ ≈ 0.99%/day.
Because the pre-holiday session is always a Thursday and Easter Monday is always a
Monday, we also test against the **same-weekday** baseline to strip out the day-of-week
confound — the Thursday-only mean is +0.0354%/day and the Monday-only mean is the usual
weak-Monday number, so the weekday control matters and is reported below.

## Pre-holiday session vs the baseline (primary spec)

| Arm | n | mean return | up-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Pre-holiday session (Maundy Thursday) | 76 | **+0.3321%** | **68.4% up** |
| Unconditional daily | ~19,100 | +0.0364% | 53.1% up |
| Unconditional Thursdays only | ~3,840 | +0.0354% | 53.3% up |

- **Excess mean: +29.6 bps/day** over the all-day baseline — about 0.30σ of a single
  day. Large for a one-day calendar window.
- **Up-rate +68.4%** vs the 53.1% base rate — the pre-holiday session is genuinely
  more often green.
- **One-sample t vs 0: t = +3.94** (p = 0.0002).
- **One-sample t vs the unconditional mean: t = +3.51** (p = 0.0008).
- **Newey-West (HAC, lag 4) t on the excess return: t = +3.28** — clears the desk's
  |t| ≥ 2 REAL hurdle.
- **Permutation p (10,000 random 76-session draws, two-sided): p = 0.012.**
- **Day-of-week control:** against the **Thursday-only** baseline the excess is still
  +29.7 bps with HAC t = **+3.29** (perm p = 0.007). The effect is **not** a weekday
  artifact — it is a genuine pre-holiday drift.

## Post-holiday session (Easter Monday) — vanishes under control

| Arm | n | mean return | up-rate | HAC t (excess) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Easter Monday vs all days | 76 | −0.1872% | 43.4% | −2.45 |
| Easter Monday vs Mondays only | 76 | −0.1872% | 43.4% | **−1.53** (perm p 0.26) |

Easter Monday looks weak against the all-day baseline, but that is just the
long-documented **Monday effect**. Against the correct **Monday-only** baseline the
excess shrinks to −14 bps with HAC t = −1.53 (perm p = 0.26) — **not** an
Easter-specific phenomenon. We report it but do not claim it.

## Sub-periods (pre-holiday excess return)

| Window | n | pre-holiday mean | excess | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1950–1979 | 30 | +27.7 bps | +24.0 bps | **+4.66** |
| 1980–2002 | 23 | +17.7 bps | +14.0 bps | +1.19 |
| 2003–2025 | 23 | +56.0 bps | +52.3 bps | **+2.39** |
| 1950–1987 | 38 | +26.7 bps | +23.1 bps | **+4.29** |
| 1988–2025 | 38 | +39.7 bps | +36.0 bps | **+2.14** |

The pre-holiday drift is **present in every coarse split** (both halves clear |t| ≥ 2),
but it is **uneven**: the middle third (1980–2002) is weak (HAC t = 1.19). A genuine but
unstable edge — robust on the whole tape, not metronomic.

## Turnover & tradability

The only implementable rule is "buy the pre-holiday session once a year" (enter at the
prior close, exit at the Maundy Thursday close — a one-session hold). Turnover is one
round-trip per year.

- **Gross mean per event: +33.2 bps.**
- **One-way cost 1 bp × NAV (round-trip 2 bps): net mean +31.2 bps/event.** The edge
  comfortably survives costs *per event* — but it fires **once a year**.
- **Compounded over 76 years: gross ×1.284, net ×1.265 — a per-event CAGR of ~0.31%.**
  Sitting in cash 364 days a year to harvest one +0.31%/yr sliver is dominated by simply
  holding the index. The capacity is enormous (it's the S&P), but the *contribution to a
  portfolio* is tiny and it cannot be levered safely on a single overnight gap.

## Positive control

On a synthetic daily tape (Mon–Fri calendar) with a **planted pre-holiday premium**, the
same engine fires cleanly: at +10 bps/day the excess is recovered with HAC t ≈ 2.9 and
permutation p ≈ 0.009; at +25 bps, HAC t ≈ 6+, p < 0.001. At premium = 0 the engine
correctly finds nothing (HAC t ≈ 0–1, p ≈ 0.5). The **real** +29.6 bps pre-holiday excess
sits above the n=76 minimum detectable effect (≈23.6 bps at 80% power) — consistent with a
real, if marginal, signal rather than a fluke.

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** Pre-holiday (Maundy Thursday) excess +29.6 bps/day, HAC t = +3.28,
  perm p = 0.012, up-rate 68%. It **survives the day-of-week control** (HAC t = +3.29 vs
  Thursdays only) and is present in both halves of the sample. This is a real **pre-holiday
  effect** — *not* Easter-specific magic; Good Friday just happens to be the holiday. Easter
  Monday adds nothing once the Monday effect is removed.
  *Signal-axis caveat:* price-only index, vendor back-revises the ^GSPC level, and
  survivorship is moot for an index level; the middle-third weakness (1980–2002) and the
  known post-publication decay of the pre-holiday effect temper the strength.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The edge is real and survives costs *per event*, but it fires
  **once a year** (~0.31% annual contribution), cannot be levered on one overnight gap, and
  the pre-holiday effect is widely known and has decayed in other markets. A genuine but
  marginal, capacity-trivial sliver — not a standalone strategy.
- **Not busted — but not Easter.** There *is* a robust seasonal here; it is the generic
  pre-long-weekend drift, present at the Good-Friday gate because Good Friday closes the NYSE.
